title: Palpation of the Chest, Shoulder and Elbow — From the Jugular Notch to the Epicondyles

hook.en: Good palpation starts from a landmark you already know and moves one step at a time. Learn the route from the jugular notch to the sternal angle, the AC joint, the coracoid and the elbow's bony points.
hook.ur: Acchi palpation us landmark se shuru hoti hai jo aap pehle se jaante hon aur ek ek qadam aage barhti hai. Jugular notch se sternal angle, AC joint, coracoid aur elbow ke bony points tak ka raasta seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll find the suprasternal notch, sternal angle, xiphoid, AC joint, coracoid process, medial and lateral epicondyles and olecranon, and say what each tells you clinically.
goal.ur: End tak aap suprasternal notch, sternal angle, xiphoid, AC joint, coracoid process, medial aur lateral epicondyles aur olecranon dhoondenge, aur batayenge ke har ek clinically kya batata hai.

text.en: Use a **chain of landmarks**: start from the one you know and slide to the next. **Jugular (suprasternal) notch** → slide down about 5 cm to the horizontal ridge of the **sternal angle** (the 2nd rib joins here, level with T4–T5) → continue to the **xiphoid** (T9–T10). For the shoulder: follow the clavicle outward to the **AC joint** (a small step at the top of the shoulder) and slide about 3 cm down and in to the **coracoid process**. At the elbow find the **medial and lateral epicondyles** and the **olecranon**.
text.ur: **Landmarks ki zanjeer** use karein: jo aap jaante hon wahan se shuru kar ke agle par slide karein. **Jugular (suprasternal) notch** → takriban 5 cm neeche **sternal angle** ki horizontal ridge (yahan 2nd rib judti hai, T4–T5 ke barabar) → **xiphoid** (T9–T10) tak. Shoulder ke liye: clavicle ko bahar ki taraf **AC joint** tak follow karein (shoulder ke top par chhota sa step) aur takriban 3 cm neeche aur andar **coracoid process** tak slide karein. Elbow par **medial aur lateral epicondyles** aur **olecranon** dhoondein.

text.en: Palpation is like walking through a town with a map: you start at the railway station (a landmark you know) and turn left at the bank, right at the mosque. If you jump straight to a random street you may get lost. Every landmark is the next one's starting point.
text.ur: Palpation naqshay ke saath shehar mein chalne jaisi hai: aap railway station (jo landmark aap jaante hain) se shuru karte hain aur bank par baayen, masjid par daayen mur'te hain. Seedha kisi bhi gali mein kood jayein to bhatak sakte hain. Har landmark agle ka starting point hai.

intro.en: From the jugular notch, slide down about 5 cm until a **horizontal ridge** appears. The 2nd costal cartilage attaches here, so you can count the ribs down from it. It is level with T4–T5 and the carina of the trachea.
intro.ur: Jugular notch se takriban 5 cm neeche slide karein jab tak **horizontal ridge** na aaye. 2nd costal cartilage yahan judti hai, is liye aap yahan se ribs ginn sakte hain. Yeh T4–T5 aur trachea ki carina ke barabar hai.

question.en: Why is the sternal angle clinically useful?
question.ur: Sternal angle clinically kyun kaam ka hai?

text.en: It marks the 2nd rib, so you can count the ribs and find the T4–T5 level
text.ur: Yeh 2nd rib ko mark karta hai, is liye aap ribs ginn kar T4–T5 level dhoond sakte hain

feedback.en: Yes — it is the best starting point for counting ribs and for auscultation landmarks.
feedback.ur: Haan — ribs ginne aur auscultation landmarks ke liye yeh behtareen starting point hai.

text.ur: Yeh xiphoid process ko mark karta hai

feedback.en: The xiphoid is the lower tip of the sternum.
feedback.ur: Xiphoid sternum ka neechla sira hai.

text.ur: Yeh pehli rib ko mark karta hai

feedback.en: The first rib is hidden under the clavicle.
feedback.ur: Pehli rib clavicle ke neeche chhupi hoti hai.

intro.en: Follow the clavicle outward until it ends in a **small step** at the top of the shoulder; the joint is about 2 cm wide. Tenderness or a step here suggests an **AC sprain**, which is common after a fall on the shoulder.
intro.ur: Clavicle ko bahar ki taraf follow karein jab tak woh shoulder ke top par **chhote step** par khatam na ho; joint takriban 2 cm chaura hai. Yahan tenderness ya step **AC sprain** batata hai jo shoulder par girne ke baad aam hai.

intro.en: From the AC joint, slide about 3 cm **down and in**, below the outer clavicle, and press firmly. A hard bony knob under the deltoid is the coracoid; it is **normally slightly tender**. Many muscles (pectoralis minor, short head of biceps, coracobrachialis) attach here.
intro.ur: AC joint se takriban 3 cm **neeche aur andar**, outer clavicle ke neeche, slide karein aur zor se dabayein. Deltoid ke neeche sakht bony knob coracoid hai; yeh **normally halka tender** hota hai. Bohat se muscles (pectoralis minor, biceps ka short head, coracobrachialis) yahan judte hain.

intro.en: Find the bony point on the outer side of the elbow above the joint line. The **common extensor tendon** attaches here, so tenderness suggests lateral epicondylalgia ("tennis elbow"). Compare with the medial epicondyle, where the common flexor tendon attaches.
intro.ur: Elbow ki bahar wali side par joint line ke upar bony point dhoondein. **Common extensor tendon** yahan judta hai, is liye tenderness lateral epicondylalgia (“tennis elbow”) batati hai. Isay medial epicondyle se compare karein jahan common flexor tendon judta hai.

title.en: Upper-body landmarks and what they tell you
title.ur: Upper body ke landmarks aur woh kya batate hain

rows.en: The soft dip at the top of the sternum between the collarbones
rows.ur: Collarbones ke beech sternum ke top par naram dip

rows.en: Midline reference; the trachea lies directly behind it
rows.ur: Midline reference; trachea iske bilkul peechay hoti hai

rows.en: The tip of the sternum where the lower ribs meet (T9–T10)
rows.ur: Sternum ki nok jahan neechli ribs milti hain (T9–T10)

rows.en: Press gently: it is cartilage and may be tender; CPR hand position landmark
rows.ur: Halka dabayein: yeh cartilage hai aur tender ho sakta hai; CPR hand position landmark

rows.en: Bony point on the inner elbow; the olecranon is the point of the elbow at the back
rows.ur: Elbow ki andar bony point; olecranon elbow ki peeth ki nok hai

rows.en: Ulnar nerve runs just behind the medial epicondyle; the three points form a line in extension and a triangle in flexion
rows.ur: Ulnar nerve medial epicondyle ke bilkul peechay chalti hai; teeno points extension mein line aur flexion mein triangle banate hain

rows.en: Follow the thumb side of the forearm to its tip at the wrist
rows.ur: Forearm ki thumb side ko kalai par uski nok tak follow karein

rows.en: About 1 cm lower than the ulnar styloid; the anatomical snuffbox is just below it (scaphoid)
rows.ur: Ulnar styloid se takriban 1 cm neeche; anatomical snuffbox iske neeche hai (scaphoid)

text.en: **Pressing too hard, too fast.** Palpating with the whole hand or pressing hard blunts your feel and makes the patient tense. Use the pads of two fingers, slow pressure and ask "is this familiar pain?" Remember also that many structures are **normally tender** (coracoid, lateral epicondyle region, the xiphoid, trigger points) so a tender spot is meaningful only if it is one-sided, reproduces the patient's familiar pain, or is bony tenderness after trauma.
text.ur: **Bohat zor se, bohat jaldi dabana.** Poore haath se palpate karne ya zor se dabane se aap ka ehsaas kund ho jata hai aur patient tense ho jata hai. Do fingers ke pads, aahista dabao use karein aur poochein “kya yeh jaana pehchana dard hai?” Yeh bhi yaad rakhein ke bohat se structures **normally tender** hote hain (coracoid, lateral epicondyle ka area, xiphoid, trigger points) is liye tender jagah tabhi mayne rakhti hai jab woh ek side ho, mareez ka jaana pehchana dard reproduce kare, ya trauma ke baad bony tenderness ho.

question.en: A patient falls on the shoulder and is tender and has a step at the top of the shoulder over the outer clavicle. Which joint is most likely injured?
question.ur: Patient shoulder par girta hai aur outer clavicle ke upar shoulder ke top par tender jagah aur step hai. Kaun sa joint sab se zyada zakhmi hai?

feedback.en: Yes — a step and tenderness at the AC joint after a fall suggests an AC sprain or separation.
feedback.ur: Haan — girne ke baad AC joint par step aur tenderness AC sprain ya separation batati hai.

feedback.en: That is at the inner end of the clavicle.
feedback.ur: Yeh clavicle ke andar wale sirey par hota hai.

feedback.en: That is deeper and not tender over the clavicle.
feedback.ur: Yeh zyada gehra hai aur clavicle ke upar tender nahi hota.

text.en: **From landmark to treatment.** Palpate to confirm a structure before you treat it: the AC joint before AC mobilisation or taping, the lateral epicondyle before tendon loading, the ulnar groove before neural gliding. Record the finding with the landmark ("tender over the right lateral epicondyle and common extensor origin, familiar pain"). For repeat measurements, such as a pressure algometer, use the same landmark and the same pressure every time.
text.ur: **Landmark se ilaaj tak.** Treat karne se pehle structure ko palpate kar ke confirm karein: AC mobilisation ya taping se pehle AC joint, tendon loading se pehle lateral epicondyle, neural gliding se pehle ulnar groove. Finding ko landmark ke saath likhein (“right lateral epicondyle aur common extensor origin par tender, jaana pehchana dard”). Dobara measurement ke liye, jaise pressure algometer, har baar wohi landmark aur wohi pressure use karein.

question.en: Why is the ulnar nerve vulnerable behind the medial epicondyle?
question.ur: Medial epicondyle ke peechay ulnar nerve vulnerable kyun hai?

answer.en: Because it runs in a shallow groove, covered only by skin and a thin fascia, with very little padding. A knock on the "funny bone" compresses the nerve against bone and causes the electric shock sensation; chronic compression there causes cubital tunnel syndrome.
answer.ur: Kyunke yeh ek uthli groove mein chalti hai, jis par sirf jild aur patli fascia hoti hai, padding bohat kam. “Funny bone” par chot nerve ko haddi ke khilaf dabati hai aur bijli jaisa jhatka deti hai; wahan musalsal dabao cubital tunnel syndrome karta hai.

question.en: Which tendon attaches at the lateral epicondyle?
question.ur: Lateral epicondyle par kaun sa tendon judta hai?

feedback.en: Yes — hence "tennis elbow" is lateral epicondylalgia.
feedback.ur: Haan — isi liye “tennis elbow” lateral epicondylalgia hai.

feedback.en: That attaches to the medial epicondyle.
feedback.ur: Yeh medial epicondyle par judta hai.

feedback.en: That is in the cubital fossa.
feedback.ur: Yeh cubital fossa mein hota hai.

text.en: **Refer urgently** for severe midline tenderness of the cervical or thoracic spine after trauma, chest pain with breathlessness or sweating (do not "palpate it away"), a hot, red, swollen joint with fever, or an elbow or shoulder deformity after a fall. Palpating a suspected fracture should be gentle and brief.
text.ur: **Foran refer karein** trauma ke baad cervical ya thoracic spine mein shadeed midline tenderness, saans phoolne ya paseenay ke saath seene ka dard (isay “palpate kar ke door” na karein), garam, laal, sooja joint bukhar ke saath, ya girne ke baad elbow ya shoulder ki deformity. Shak-e-fracture ko halke aur mukhtasar palpate karein.

summary.en: Palpate in a chain from a known landmark: notch → sternal angle → xiphoid; clavicle → AC joint → coracoid; elbow epicondyles and olecranon.
summary.ur: Known landmark se zanjeer mein palpate karein: notch → sternal angle → xiphoid; clavicle → AC joint → coracoid; elbow ke epicondyles aur olecranon.

summary.en: Each landmark has a clinical use: rib counting, AC sprain, tendon origins (common extensor and flexor) and the ulnar nerve.
summary.ur: Har landmark ka clinical istemal hai: ribs ginna, AC sprain, tendon origins (common extensor aur flexor) aur ulnar nerve.

summary.en: Use light, slow pressure; many structures are normally tender, so one-sided, familiar or post-traumatic tenderness is what counts.
summary.ur: Halka, aahista dabao use karein; bohat se structures normally tender hain, is liye ek side, jaana pehchana ya trauma ke baad ki tenderness mayne rakhti hai.

front.en: Where do you find the sternal angle?

back.en: About 5 cm below the jugular notch as a horizontal ridge; the 2nd rib joins here (level with T4–T5).
back.ur: Jugular notch se takriban 5 cm neeche horizontal ridge; yahan 2nd rib judti hai (T4–T5 ke barabar).

front.en: What is tender over the lateral epicondyle in tennis elbow?
front.ur: Tennis elbow mein lateral epicondyle par kya tender hota hai?

front.en: Which nerve lies behind the medial epicondyle?
front.ur: Medial epicondyle ke peechay kaun si nerve hoti hai?

front.en: What does a step at the AC joint suggest?
front.ur: AC joint par step kya batata hai?

back.en: An AC joint sprain or separation.
